text_simplified: The text discusses a noble hadith that clarifies the best gift a parent can give their child is good adab (manners) and sound tarbiyah (upbringing). It also highlights the importance of justice among children and not favoring one over another. It urges taqwa (God-consciousness) in dealing with one’s children.

review_defects.why: Arabic 'التأديب' (at-ta'deeb) means disciplining/teaching good behavior, not 'adab' (manners). The translation uses the wrong Islamic term, changing the gift from an action to a quality.
Same error as title: 'التأديب' is disciplining, not 'adab'. The parenthetical '(manners)' reinforces the wrong meaning.
Arabic 'الوالد' specifically means father, not the gender-neutral 'parent'. The hadith refers to a father's gift to his child.
Arabic explicitly says 'Prophetic noble hadith' (نبوي); English 'noble hadith' omits 'Prophetic', softening the attribution.
Arabic 'صالحة' means righteous/pious, not merely 'sound'. The translation loses the religious connotation.
